title: Benchmarking and Evolving Reason-Reflect-Rectify for Reflective Visual Generation
claim: Existing generators and reflective models diagnose errors well but fail to correct them; our RL loop uses reflection as reward to fix rectification.
layout: 3 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, colored banners, image gallery then flow then loop
description: A three-row figure with color-coded banner titles. Panel (a), on an orange banner, shows five generated photos in a row, each under a red error label (Shape, Texture, Color, Spatial, Count) with its prompt below, such as a teardrop earring or a cup left of a horse. Panel (b), on a blue banner, shows a flawed image of an apple with a vase prompt. It goes through a brain-icon 'Current MLLM/UMM', which splits into a green checked Reflection box (correct diagnosis) and a red crossed Rectification box (bad fix). A resulting wrong image is marked with an X. Scores of 72.0 and 38.0 are shown, with 'Capability Misalignment' in red. Panel (c), on a green banner, shows a cyclic RL diagram with input prompt+image, R³-bench evaluation, an editor, a trajectory, a self-reflective reward and an RL optimizer. Orange arrows carry the policy update back to the model.
caption: (a) Existing text-to-image (T2I) models often struggle with compositional prompts, resulting in diverse visual generation errors. (b) Reflective visual generation aims to mitigate these errors, yet current models suffer from a capability misalignment: they accurately diagnose flaws (strong reasoning) but fail to execute valid corrections (weak rectification). (c) To bridge this gap, we introduce R$^3$-Bench and R$^3$-Refiner, a reinforcement learning framework that leverages the model's strong reasoning as a self-reflective reward to optimize rectification policies.
abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) models and Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) have achieved remarkable progress in visual generation. However, their reliance on a single-pass generation paradigm limits their ability to handle complex prompts requiring iterative refinement. To enable multi-round Reflective Visual Generation (RVG), we formalize the Reason-Reflect-Rectify (R^3) loop as a core framework and introduce R^3-Bench, a benchmark of over 600 expert-annotated instances that quantifies iterative reasoning and rectification capabilities. Evaluation on R^3-Bench reveals a critical gap: while state-of-the-art models can identify generation errors, they fail to generate actionable rectification instructions. To bridge this gap, we propose R^3-Refiner, a dual-stage framework leveraging Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and a Hierarchical Reward Mechanism (HRM) to better align rectification with reflective reasoning. Experiments show that R^3-Refiner achieves significant improvements on R^3-Bench (+12.0% in Reflective Verdict Score, +9.0% in Rectification Score), and can be seamlessly integrated with various MLLMs to enhance the generation quality of different T2I models on GenEval++ and T2I-CompBench. Code is available at https://github.com/xiaomoguhz/R3-Bench.
